$$

$$

 we must have

$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-2y & -2x \\ -2x & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,-1).$" :question/worked-solution "For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{2} & 2y{x}^{2}-1\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x{y}^{2},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2y{x}^{2}-1.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2})=2{y}^{2}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y{x}^{2}-1)=4xy \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2})=4xy\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y{x}^{2}-1)=2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2} & 4xy \\ 4xy & 2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(1,-1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,-1)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(1,-1)=2\cdot 2-(-4)\cdot (-4)=-12.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-835cf471-5984-50ad-ac7a-5c92395f40c6"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-835cf471-5984-50ad-ac7a-5c92395f40c6" :answer-field/id #uuid "835cf471-5984-50ad-ac7a-5c92395f40c6" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-012e8862-6d84-5ca3-808d-e580b5b68412" :answer-field/choices ["answer-012e8862-6d84-5ca3-808d-e580b5b68412" "answer-1d97894b-06e8-5458-afce-3b6280583bcd" "answer-6341ade3-f46e-594c-b2db-483df7d6f5cd" "answer-49af7f88-d313-53b2-a836-26eef4f823e6" "answer-e9393f5b-f485-5c2a-b52d-4ac15221029b"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-012e8862-6d84-5ca3-808d-e580b5b68412" :answer/id #uuid "012e8862-6d84-5ca3-808d-e580b5b68412" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-12" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1d97894b-06e8-5458-afce-3b6280583bcd" :answer/id #uuid "1d97894b-06e8-5458-afce-3b6280583bcd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-8" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6341ade3-f46e-594c-b2db-483df7d6f5cd" :answer/id #uuid "6341ade3-f46e-594c-b2db-483df7d6f5cd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "12" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-49af7f88-d313-53b2-a836-26eef4f823e6" :answer/id #uuid "49af7f88-d313-53b2-a836-26eef4f823e6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "20" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e9393f5b-f485-5c2a-b52d-4ac15221029b" :answer/id #uuid "e9393f5b-f485-5c2a-b52d-4ac15221029b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]}]

evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,-1).$"] ["question-e525b492-a29a-585f-8c96-2055a51f2341" :question/worked-solution "For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{2} & 2y{x}^{2}-1\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x{y}^{2},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2y{x}^{2}-1.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2})=2{y}^{2}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y{x}^{2}-1)=4xy \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2})=4xy\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y{x}^{2}-1)=2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2} & 4xy \\ 4xy & 2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(1,-1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,-1)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(1,-1)=2\cdot 2-(-4)\cdot (-4)=-12.
$$"] ["question-e525b492-a29a-585f-8c96-2055a51f2341" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["answer-field-835cf471-5984-50ad-ac7a-5c92395f40c6" :answer-field/id #uuid The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(\mathbf x) = \det \left( \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x) \right)
$$

In our case, we have

![](images/14/1488754e319066706880b21fd4642c7b6a75a458770cab254b974b13d35425a2.svg)

First, notice that since ![](images/c9/c92e0f35c58187af3fe961947e6e96f0cd82cf32bb00cfd4f51ca3c742339e0c.svg) we must have

$$
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} = \ln y, 
\qquad 
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} = \dfrac xy.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{y})=\frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=\frac{1}{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{y})=-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(0,1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0,1)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(0,1) = 0 \cdot 0 - 1\cdot 1 = -1.
$$"} {:db/id 17592186049044} {:db/id 17592186157792 :question/id #uuid "56bfdc28-d81a-5ee4-a9f9-1fab676af72b" :question/math-academy-id "q-80944"} {:db/id 17592186157793 :question/id #uuid evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,0).$" :question/worked-solution "For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+6x-4y & 4{y}^{3}-4x+8y\end{aligned}],$
we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=3{x}^{2}+6x-4y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=4{y}^{3}-4x+8y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}+6x-4y)=6x+6\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{y}^{3}-4x+8y)=-4 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}+6x-4y)=-4\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4{y}^{3}-4x+8y)=12{y}^{2}+8\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6x+6 & -4 \\ -4 & 12{y}^{2}+8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(1,0),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,0)=[\begin{aligned}12 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(1,0)=12\cdot 8-(-4)\cdot (-4)=80.
$$"} {:db/id 17592186284390 :question/id #uuid "64116d30-10df-5392-b872-327ec4131913" :question/math-academy-id "q-163642"} {:db/id 17592186284391 :question/id #uuid $$

$$

$$
